cards.text: The psalmist is still talking to the LORD, and this part opens with something personal: he says God's own hands made him and fashioned him. The Millers, my old family, carved my name into my handle ONE time, and I still bring it up to every baker who walks in. This man says he was shaped by the hands of God Himself!

cards.question: So the psalmist turns to the One who made him. What does he ask his Maker to give him?

answers.text: Strength to defeat all his enemies
Riches to take care of his family

cards.text: Then he tells the LORD he wants the people who fear Him to see him and rejoice. When I walk into a room, the only thing that lights up is the oven, and that's because I turned it ON.

cards.question: The psalmist asks that those who fear God would see him and rejoice, because he has hoped in God's ___.

cards.text: Then he says he knows the LORD's judgments are righteous. And he says something about his own hard times, too.

cards.question: The psalmist says the LORD afflicted him in faithfulness.

cards.text: Then he asks for the LORD's loving devotion to comfort him, according to His promise to His servant. He's not asking for anything new, friend, just what God already promised.

cards.question: Next, the psalmist asks for the LORD's compassion to come to him. What does he want it to do for him?
In that same breath, the psalmist calls God's law his ___.

cards.text: Then he brings up the arrogant, who are subverting him with a lie, and he asks that they be put to shame. Somebody spreads a lie about ME, I'm in the group chat typing in ALL CAPS for an hour.

cards.question: With the arrogant lying about him, what does the psalmist say he will do?
The psalmist asks that people who know God's testimonies would turn away from him.

cards.text: The last line of this stretch is about his own heart. He asks that it be blameless in God's statutes.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist want his heart to be blameless in God's statutes?

answers.text: So he won't be put to shame
So kings will give him honor
So he'll grow rich in old age

cards.text: The next stretch starts heavy: the psalmist's soul faints for God's salvation, and he's waiting for God's word. Friend, I can't wait twelve minutes on a batch without pressing my whole mustache against the oven window.

cards.question: The psalmist's eyes fail from looking for God's promise. What does he ask the LORD while he waits?

answers.text: Why did You ever make me
Where have You gone to now

cards.text: Then he says he's like a wineskin dried up by smoke. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so I know that look.

cards.question: Dried up like a wineskin in the smoke, the psalmist says he has forgotten God's statutes.
Still waiting, the psalmist asks the LORD how many days His servant must wait. What else does he want to know?

answers.text: When God will judge his persecutors
Why his closest friends have left him
Where his family has been taken to

cards.text: And it gets worse. Now the arrogant have dug pits for him, in violation of God's law.
He tells the LORD all His commandments are faithful, and then he cries out, "help me!" Sometimes that's the whole prayer, friend.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist say he is being persecuted?

answers.text: There's no cause for it at all
He broke one of the king's laws
He stole land from his neighbor

cards.text: Then he says they almost wiped him from the earth. I bet that one hurt.

cards.question: Even after nearly being wiped from the earth, the psalmist says he has not forsaken God's precepts.
The psalmist ends this stretch asking the LORD to ___ him according to His loving devotion, so he can ___ the testimony of God's mouth.

cards.text: Then, friend, the mood shifts. After two stretches of liars, pits and waiting, the psalmist calls out to the LORD and says something BIG about His word.

cards.question: What does the psalmist say about the LORD's word?

answers.text: It is everlasting and fixed in the heavens
It is hidden and hard for anyone to find
It is only for the priests in the temple

cards.text: He says the LORD's faithfulness continues through ALL generations. I can't keep a New Year's resolution through ONE January.

cards.question: The psalmist says the LORD established the earth, but it won't last.

cards.text: Then he says God's ordinances stand "to this day," still standing when he wrote it. Not stood, friend. STAND.

cards.question: The psalmist says God's ordinances still stand, because all things are His ___.
The psalmist looks back on his hard times. If God's law hadn't been his delight, what does he say would have happened?

answers.text: He would have perished in his affliction
He would have run away from his enemies
He would have turned his back on God

cards.question: The psalmist says God has given him new life through His precepts.
The psalmist tells the LORD he belongs to Him. What does he ask the LORD to do?

cards.text: He says the wicked are waiting to destroy him, but he will ponder God's testimonies. Same move he made when the arrogant lied about him.
Last line of this stretch: he says he has seen a limit to all perfection. Tell me about it, friend, my edges went soft YEARS ago in the Millers' kitchen.

cards.question: The psalmist says God's commandment has a limit too.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this one on the cooling rack. Don't go anywhere, friend, this psalm still has more to say.
